title: Polynomial entanglement lower bounds for explicit f-routing tasks
statement: Find an explicit family of Boolean functions f_n on two n-bit inputs for which any bounded-error f-routing protocol needs an entangled resource of cost at least n^c for some fixed c>0. Alice initially holds an unknown quantum system Q; after input-dependent local operations, one simultaneous exchange of quantum messages and local decoding, Q must be recovered by Alice or Bob according to f_n(x,y), preserving its entanglement with an arbitrary reference.
assumptions: Use the communication pattern and logarithmic local-dimension resource cost in IQOQI Problem 48; unrestricted extra communication would change the task.
Fix a nontrivial small constant diamond-norm error tolerance independent of n and require correctness for every input pair.
The lower bound should hold for general allowed quantum operations and an explicit function family, not merely random functions or a one-sided-perfect protocol.
physics_motivation: Quantifies the entanglement needed to imitate a nonlocal quantum interaction and underpins security bounds for quantum position verification.
resolution_target: An explicit family and a rigorous polynomial lower bound on the preshared entanglement resource at fixed error, or a general upper bound ruling out that target.
status_note: Alex May's IQOQI Problem 48 (listed January 2026) asks for this lower bound. The 2026 journal version of the cited NLQC paper establishes reductions and partial bounds, not the stated general explicit-family lower bound. Source statement and paper metadata/abstract were checked; this is not a complete later-citation audit.

relations.note: Both concern limits of certifying quantum behavior, but position verification and computation verification have different resources and adversaries.

title: One-shot work and coherence cost of Gibbs-preserving channels
statement: For a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian H and a quantum channel Phi satisfying Phi(gamma_beta)=gamma_beta, determine the minimal work and time-translation-asymmetry resources needed to implement Phi, within a specified error, using energy-conserving unitaries, thermal ancillas and explicit resource systems. Seek matching achievable resource costs and converse bounds for general inputs, including coherent inputs.
assumptions: Freeze the battery model, coherence or clock resource, allowed ancilla Hamiltonians, and whether catalysts must be returned exactly, approximately or uncorrelated.
Specify a channel error criterion such as diamond distance rather than only reproducing the action on one input state.
Use a single-shot implementation with a nontrivial system Hamiltonian; asymptotic state conversion and zero-Hamiltonian results are separate regimes.
physics_motivation: Explains what physical thermodynamic resources are hidden when Gibbs-preserving maps are treated as free operations.
resolution_target: A resource-cost characterization with matching protocols and lower bounds under the chosen implementation rules, including the dependence on accuracy.
status_note: Philippe Faist's IQOQI Problem 46 distinguishes general Gibbs-preserving maps from thermal operations and describes solved restricted cases. The resource conventions are part of the question; this entry does not claim that all thermal-operation or covariant-channel implementation problems remain open.

title: Complexity of constant-trace-distance quantum separability testing
aliases: Constant-error weak membership for separable states
statement: Determine the computational complexity, as local dimension d grows, of distinguishing a separable density matrix on C^d tensor C^d from one at least epsilon away from every separable state in trace distance, for fixed epsilon>0 and a promised gap. In particular, determine whether a quasipolynomial-time classical algorithm is possible in the explicit-matrix input model.
assumptions: Input consists of finite-precision rational matrix entries with a bit-length promise; use trace distance one half of the trace norm consistently.
The gap epsilon is fixed independently of d; inverse-polynomial precision is a different established hardness regime.
Do not replace trace distance by a local-measurement or LOCC distinguishability norm.
physics_motivation: Asks how efficiently entanglement can be certified from a quantum state's full classical description, and constrains the power of unentangled quantum witnesses.
resolution_target: A proved constant-gap algorithm with dimension and precision complexity bounds, or a conditional hardness result excluding a specified runtime under explicit assumptions.
status_note: Henry Yuen's IQOQI Problem 44 separates inverse-polynomial-error hardness and algorithms for weaker distinguishability norms from the trace-distance target. The current source statement was checked; later complexity results have not been exhaustively audited.

sources.title: Henry Yuen: Complexity of the separability problem — IQOQI Problem 44

relations.note: Algorithmic testing of a given state differs from characterizing every state with a fixed spectrum.
Both connect quantum states to complexity, but their promise problems and physical inputs differ.

title: Does every bipartite entangled state have positive distillable secret key?
statement: For finite-dimensional bipartite entangled states rho_AB, determine whether the asymptotic distillable secret-key rate under local quantum operations and authenticated public classical communication is always strictly positive, when the eavesdropper holds a purification. Alternatively, construct an entangled state and prove that its unrestricted two-way distillable key is zero.
assumptions: Allow arbitrarily many independent copies and general two-way public communication.
The security criterion requires an asymptotically uniform shared key independent of the eavesdropper and transcript.
A zero one-way rate, failure of one protocol, or zero singlet-distillation rate is not sufficient for a negative answer.
physics_motivation: Determines whether all quantum entanglement has an asymptotically usable secrecy resource, including states with no distillable singlets.
resolution_target: A positive-rate distillation argument for every entangled state, or an explicit entangled state with an all-protocol zero-key converse.
status_note: Paweł Horodecki's IQOQI Problem 24 records the general question and partial constructions of key from bound entanglement. Those constructions do not establish positivity for every state. The open-list entry and its distinctions were checked, not the full subsequent literature.

sources.title: Paweł Horodecki: Secret key from all entangled states — IQOQI Problem 24
Horodecki, Horodecki, Horodecki and Oppenheim: Secure key from bound entanglement

relations.note: Secret key and singlet distillation are different resources; PPT states can have positive key.
Entanglement swapping and repeater usefulness impose additional constraints beyond key extraction.

title: Spectral characterization of absolute separability beyond qubit–qudit systems
statement: For bipartite dimensions m,n at least three, characterize the eigenvalue lists for which every density matrix with that spectrum is separable across the fixed m by n partition. Determine whether absolute positive-partial-transpose spectra already suffice, or characterize the additional restrictions required for absolute separability.
assumptions: Equivalently, require U rho U† to be separable for every global unitary U; no restriction to local unitaries.
Keep the local dimensions fixed when defining the spectral set.
The target concerns deterministic absolute separability, not complete absolute separability under the probabilistic operations in the 2026 paper.
physics_motivation: Determines when a state's mixedness prevents any global unitary from generating bipartite entanglement.
resolution_target: Necessary and sufficient spectral conditions in the stated dimensions, or a certified separation between absolute PPT and absolute separability with the remaining characterization made explicit.
status_note: IQOQI Problem 15 describes the solved qubit–qudit case and the 2026 characterization of the different, complete-absolute-separability class. The latter paper's abstract was checked to avoid importing its solved variant as the open target. General deterministic higher-dimensional classification remains the provisional scope here.

title: Tensor-stable weak positivity beyond strongly positive decoherence functionals
statement: In the joint-measurement-history framework of IQOQI Problem 36, determine whether a normalized Hermitian decoherence functional D can fail positive semidefiniteness while every tensor power D^{tensor n} remains weakly positive on all event-indicator vectors. Require D to satisfy the framework's decoherence constraints for each feasible measurement partition.
assumptions: Weak positivity tests indicator vectors of all history events; strong positivity tests arbitrary complex vectors.
Fix the history space and feasible measurement partitions, and preserve the normalization and decoherence axioms under independent composition.
One fixed functional must work for every n; a different functional for each finite n is insufficient.
Do not demand a tensor-closed family containing all strongly positive functionals: the source explains an obstruction to that stronger extension.
physics_motivation: Tests whether composability alone forces a quantum-like positivity axiom in histories-based formulations motivated partly by quantum gravity.
resolution_target: An explicit admissible non-PSD functional with an all-tensor-power weak-positivity proof, or a theorem excluding one under the same axioms.
status_note: Miguel Navascués' IQOQI Problem 36 distinguishes tensor-power stability from finite-copy constructions and from extensions containing the whole strongly positive cone. This is a mathematical consistency problem, not a request for laboratory validation. The source was checked; later resolutions have not been comprehensively surveyed.
